Where things stand

A spa people love, with nowhere online to book it

Boat House Spa has 4.5 stars from 80 Google reviews, close to 4,000 followers on Facebook and a beautiful new photo shoot. But there's no website, so everyone who wants a treatment has to call, send a WhatsApp or walk in, and wait for an answer.

What a guest finds today

  • No website. Your Google listing shows "Add website", so the people searching for a spa in Beau Vallon get your phone number and nothing to book with.
  • No way to see a free time. Your hair menu asks guests to book one to two weeks ahead, but nobody can see which days are still open. They message, wait for a reply, and try another day.
  • Every booking goes through the front desk. Calls and WhatsApps come in while the team is with clients, and in the evening when the spa is closed.

The directory page speaks for you

  • It lists treatments you don't offer. The KOEK page talks about a "Sea Breeze Massage", a "Luminous Pearl Infusion" and a "Romantic Sunset Serenade". Your real menu and prices aren't on it.
  • It shows an old WhatsApp number, 2 804 100, not the 2 734 734 on all your posts, and the contact details sit behind a "Show contacts" button.
  • Your opening hours are different from post to post, so guests can't be sure when you're open.
  • The new photos of the spa are only on Facebook, where they slip down the page within a few weeks.
Why a website matters for a spa

What a great site does for Boat House Spa

A spa treatment is often booked on a whim: on a sunbed across the road, in a hotel room the night before, or on the plane. A website with online booking turns that moment into an appointment in your diary.

Bookings at any hour

Your diary fills while you work

Guests pick a treatment, a therapist and a free time by themselves. Bookings come in at 10 pm and during a 90-minute massage, without anyone picking up the phone.

Visitors across the road

Beau Vallon's hotels are full of people searching "spa near me"

Visitors book from home before they fly, or on their phone on the beach. A site gives Google your treatments, prices, hours and a Book button to show them.

Fewer messages

Answers before they ask

Prices, treatment lengths, opening hours, directions and the resident discount are all on the site, so the WhatsApps you get are bookings, not questions.

Full diaries, planned

See who's coming, days ahead

Because guests can see what's free, the quiet days fill up too. Hair appointments that need two weeks' notice get booked two weeks ahead.

First impressions

A site that feels like the spa

Glass on three sides, trees all around, white towels and a red hibiscus. The site carries the same calm, so guests arrive already relaxed and the price makes sense.

Your own address

Somewhere to send everyone

Your Instagram bio, Facebook posts, Google Maps and gift vouchers can all point to one address with the menu, the photos and a way to book.

The new site

Calm, slow, and a little bit surprising

Most spa websites look alike: a photo of stones and a bamboo stalk. This one is built on large, elegant type and your own photos, with small moments of movement that make people slow down as they scroll: a headline that rises in letter by letter, a window onto your treatment room that opens to fill the screen, and a sentence that lights up as you read it.

The full site is live for you to try. Open it on your phone, look through the treatments and book one from start to finish. It's on a private preview address and isn't listed on Google.

Open the live site

Step inside as you scroll

"Slow is a place." rises in letter by letter beside a pebble-shaped window onto your treatment room. As you scroll, the pebble opens until the room fills the screen, the headline drifts away, and a single line comes in: glass on three sides, trees all around, the bay just below.

One slow breath

Halfway down the page, the site asks visitors to take a breath with it: in for four, hold for two, out for six. The word swells and softens while a ring grows and shrinks.

It takes twelve seconds, and it's the moment people remember and show their friends.

Treatments in big, simple type

Massage, nails, facials, for two, waxing and hair, each with a short line and its starting price. On a computer, a photo of that treatment follows the cursor; on a phone, each one has a small photo beside it.

Your photos, up the steps

Your new photo shoot gets the space it deserves: the steps up from the beach road, the balcony, the polish cart, the couples room. The row slides sideways as you scroll down.

We'd only put them live with your OK.

The whole menu, as text

All 48 treatments from your price and hair menus are typed up, with their lengths and prices in rupees. They're easy to read on any phone, and Google can find them.

Every treatment has its own Book button, and the resident 20% off is shown on every page.

The site is designed for phones first, because that's where most visitors will find it. Visitors who've turned off animations on their phone get the same site, calm and still.

The centrepiece

Online booking, in four steps

Booking is the heart of the site. Guests see real free times, pick one and get a confirmation, all in about a minute. Nothing changes at the spa: they still pay when they come in.

Treatment

Choose what you'd like

From the menu or straight on the booking page, with the length and price. Couples treatments book two therapists at once.

Therapist

Someone you know, or the first free

Regulars can ask for Tina or Samantha, and each name shows their next free time.

Time

Only times that really work

Three weeks of days, marked "full" or "few left". A time only shows if the whole treatment fits before closing.

Details

Name, mobile, done

A note for allergies or a nail colour, and a tick box for the resident discount, which takes 20% off the total.

"Free soon", right on the home page

The home page shows a few of the next open times. Tap one and the guest goes straight to their details, with the treatment and time already filled in. It's the quickest way to fill a gap in tomorrow's diary.

A confirmation they'll keep

Guests get a booking reference and the amount to pay at the spa, and can add the appointment to their phone's calendar with a reminder. A "Send these details on WhatsApp" button is there for anyone who prefers to message.

How bookings reach your team

In the live site, the booking screens connect to a booking calendar your team can open on their phones, so a booking made online appears straight away and nobody gets double-booked. You'd get a WhatsApp or email for each new booking. We'll talk through the options on the call and set up the one that suits you:

A salon booking app

Tools such as Fresha or SimplyBook.me give each therapist a calendar app and can add a Book button to your Google listing. Our booking screens sit in front of it.

Square Appointments

A good choice if you'd like to take card deposits for some treatments, such as couples packages or keratin.

Your own calendar

A shared Google Calendar for each therapist, connected to the site. No monthly app fee, and we look after it for you.

Start simple

Prefer to confirm each booking yourselves first? The site can send every request to your WhatsApp, and you reply to confirm.

The demo you can try uses sample free times, and no booking is sent anywhere yet.

Questions

Things you might be wondering

Will online booking mean double bookings?

No. The site only shows times that are really free in your booking calendar, and walk-ins or phone bookings you add there disappear from the site straight away.

Can guests still call or WhatsApp?

Of course. Your phone and WhatsApp numbers are on every page, and many regulars will keep messaging. The site simply gives everyone else a way to book too.

Do we have to take payments online?

No. Guests pay at the spa, as they do now. Card deposits for some treatments can be added later if you ever want them.

What about the resident discount?

Guests tick "I live in Seychelles" and see the price with 20% off. You check as you do today when they come in.

How do we change prices or treatments?

Send us the changes on WhatsApp or by email and we'll update the site. We'll talk through an aftercare option on the call, so updates are always quick.

Where do the photos and reviews come from?

The photos are from your public Facebook page, and the review lines and rating are from Google. We'd only put them live with your OK.

What if we want something different from the concept?

Tell us on the call. Small changes are free once you buy the site, and anything bigger is quoted before we start, so there are no surprises.
